record.title: Conjecture on the Haagerup graphs $\Gamma_k$ as principal graphs
record.statement: Let $\Gamma_k$ denote the graphs in the paper's Figure 2. **Haagerup graph principal-graph conjecture.** For every $k>1$, the graph $\Gamma_k$ is not a principal graph of a subfactor. The paper proves this for $13\geq k>1$ and indicates that the same conclusion is very likely for $19\geq k>13$, conditional on the irreducibility issue; the assertion for all $k>1$ remains open.
record.source_name: Marta Asaeda, “Galois groups and an obstruction to principal graphs of subfactors”, arXiv:math/0605318 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605318

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2006).

record.title: Non-APN conjecture for the functions $f_{b,c,r}$
record.statement: Let $m\ge 8$ be an even integer, let $b,c\in\mathbb{F}_{2^m}$, and let $r$ satisfy $r\le m/2$ and $\gcd(r,m)=1$. Let $f_{b,c,r}$ denote the function defined in Theorem. **Non-APN conjecture.** For every such choice of $b,c,r$, the function $f_{b,c,r}$ is not APN. The preceding computer checks establish this claim for $8\le m\le 22$ under the stated conditions, while the general case remains open.

record.title: Ordered Ramsey numbers
record.statement:
Does there exist $\epsilon > 0$ such that $r_<(K_3,M) = O(n^{2-\epsilon})$ for every ordered matching $M$ on $n$ vertices.

\emph{Known:} $r_<(K_3, M) \le r_< (K_3, K_n) = \Theta(n^2/\log n)$.

\emph{Known:} There exists an ordered matching $M$ on $n$ vertices such that $r_<(K_3, M) = n^{4/3 + o(1)}$.

\textbf{Question:} Does there exist a constant $c > 0$ such that for every sufficiently large $n$ there exists a 100-regular graph $H$ on $n$ vertices such that $r_<(H) \ge n^{1 + c}$ for every ordering of $H$?

record.title: Ehrhart $h^\ast$-polynomial: Unimodality and Real-Rootedness (problem 6)
record.statement:
Consider the order polynomial, denoted $\Omega(P,t)$, of a finite poset $P$. Let $n$ be the number of elements in $P$. 

\textbf{Conjecture} [Kahn, Saks] $\frac{\Omega(P,t)}{t^n}$ is nonincreasing for all $t\in {\\mathbb{Z}}_{>0}$.

This statement is known to be true if all coefficients of $\Omega(P,t)$ are positive. Investigate the conjecture more generally.

(See solution to Exercise 3.163(b) in \texttt{Enumerative Combinatorics Vol.~1} by Stanley).

record.title: Rigidity (problem 5)
record.statement:
Is it possible to strengthen a theorem of Walter Whiteley (in A matroid on hypergraphs with applications in scene analysis and geometry, 1989)
on body-pin frameworks in $d=2$, to say that $G=(B, J, I)$ has an independent realization in

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.53
record.statement: In the notation of 21.52, let $\operatorname{Aut}_t(\Gamma)$ be the set of permutations $\tau\in S_D$ such that $(a,b)\sim(a^\tau,b^\tau)$ whenever $|ab|=t$ for $a,b\in D$. Clearly, $\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)=\bigcap_t\operatorname{Aut}_t(\Gamma)$. Is it true that for every finite simple group $G$ we have $\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)=\operatorname{Aut}_2(\Gamma)\cap\operatorname{Aut}_p(\Gamma)$, where $\{2,p\}$ are the two minimal prime divisors of $|G|$?

record.title: Algebraic Stories — Ideals of generic forms
record.statement: [Fr\"oberg's Conjecture, 1985] Let $f_1, \dots, f_r$ be generic forms of degrees $d_1, \dots, d_r$, respectively. Then the Hilbert series of the quotient algebra $R = S/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ is given by $$ \operatorname{Hilb}_R(t)=\left[\frac{\prod_{i=1}^r(1-t^{d_i})}{(1-t)^n}\right]_+. $$ Here $[\sum_{i\ge0}a_iz^i]_+:=\sum_{i\ge0}b_iz^i$, with $b_i=a_i$ if $a_j\ge0$ for all $j\le i$ and $b_i=0$. In other words, $[\sum_{i\ge0}a_iz^i]_+$ is the truncation of a power series at its first non-positive coefficient.
record.source_name: Fröberg, Lundqvist, Oneto, Shapiro - Algebraic Stories from One and from the Other Pockets (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.25
record.statement: In the opposite direction to Problem 1.24, does there exist a meromorphic function such that for every pair of distinct values $a, b$, we have \[\limsup_{r\to\infty}\frac{n(r,a)}{n(r,b)}=\infty\hspace{1cm}\text{ and }\hspace{1cm}\liminf_{r\to\infty}\frac{n(r,a)}{n(r,b)}=0.\] Note, of course, that either of the above limits for all distinct $a, b$ implies the other. (Compare the result (1.3) quoted in Problem 1.2, which shows that this certainly cannot occur for the $N$-function.) The above question can also be asked for entire functions. (P. Erd\"os)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 5.7
record.statement: If $c_k$ is a sequence of positive numbers such that \[\sum c_k=S<+\infty,\] and $n_k$ is an arbitrary sequence of positive integers, then \[f(z)=\sum^\infty_{n=0}c_kz^{n_k}=\sum^\infty_{n=0}a_nz^n\] is bounded in $\mathbb{D}$, and so takes no values outside a fixed disc. This shows that no conditions on the omitted values $w$ can imply more than $$ a_n=o(1). $$ Clearly ([source label: 5.10]) holds if $f(z)$ is bounded, since then \[I_2(r,f)=\Big(\sum^\infty_{n=0}|a_n|^2\Big)^{\frac{1}{2}}<+\infty.\] It would be of interest to obtain a non-trivial condition on the values omitted by $f(z)$, which would imply ([source label: 5.10]). Such a condition might be $d(r)\to0$, where $d(r)$ is defined as in Problem 5.5.
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.5
record.statement: If it proves too difficult to obtain sharp bounds for all of the coefficients in Problem 6.4, we ask for the orders of magnitude. An area principle shows that \[\sum^\infty_{n=1}n|b_n|^2\leq1\] and hence \[b_n=o(n^{-\frac{1}{2}}).\] Clunie and Pommerenke have shown that \[|b_n|=O(n^{-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{300}}).\] In the opposite direction, examples due to Clunie show that \[|b_n|>n^{-1+\delta}\] is possible for indefinitely many $n$ and a fixed $F(z)$ in $\Sigma$, where $\delta$ is an absolute constant.

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.84
record.statement: If $f(z)$ in $S$, write \[\log\frac{f(z)}{z}=2\sum^\infty_{n=1}\gamma_nz^n\] and \[f(z^p)^{1/p}=z+\sum^\infty_{n=1}c^{(p)}_nz^{pn+1}\hspace{1cm}(p=1,2,\ldots).\] Szeg\"o's conjecture asserts that $c^{(p)}_n=O(n^{2/p-1})$ as $n\to\infty$. This has been proved for $p = 1,2$ and $3$, but Pommerenke has shown that it is false for $p\geq 12$; his example also has $\gamma_n\neq O(1/n)$. Milin has shown that, if a function $f$ in $S$ has the property that $\gamma_n=O(1/n)$, then $c^{(p)}_n=O(n^{2/p-1})$ for every $p$. Is the converse true? (P. L. Duren)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.113
record.statement: Following the notation of Problem 6.111 and 6.112, it is known that, if $|x|\leq\rho\leq1$ and $\gamma=1/(1+\rho)^2$, then \[N_\gamma\Big(\frac{z}{1-xz}\Big)\subset S^*.\] Is it true that \[\Sigma_\gamma\Big(\frac{z}{1-xz}\Big)\subset S^*?\] Notice that, since not all convex functions belong to $S^*$ (see Sheil-Small and Silvia ), it follows that we cannot replace in the above, $N_\gamma(z/(1-xz))$ by $N_\gamma(g)$, where $g$ is an arbitrary convex function. (T. Sheil-Small and E. M. Silvia)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.72
record.statement: Let $N$ denote the class of complex-valued $L^\infty$-functions $v$ on the unit disc $U$ such that $\int_U v\phi\,dx\,dy=0$ whenever $\phi$ is analytic in $U$ with $\int_U|\phi(x+iy)|\,dx\,dy<\infty$. The Cauchy principal value of \[(Bv)(z)=\frac{-1}{\pi}\int_U\frac{v(\zeta)}{(z-\zeta)^2}\,d\xi\,d\eta,\hspace{1cm}\zeta=\xi+i\eta,\] defines the Beurling transform $Bv$ of $v$. Is it true that $Bv\in L^\infty$ and, furthermore, that $$ \|Bv\|_\infty\leq C\|v\|_\infty, $$ for some $C < \infty$, whenever $v\in N$. A weaker question is whether this holds for all $v\in N\cap P$, where $P$ is the class of all polynomials in $z$ and $\overline{z}$. (The inequality ([source label: K7.72]) is true at least for certain subclasses of $N\cap P$.) (A. Hinkkanen)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 8.11
record.statement: Let $g$ be a function in the space $D$ of functions analytic in $|z|< 1$ with finite Dirichlet integral, i.e., \[{\int\int}_{|z|<1}|h'(z)|^2\,dx\,dy<\infty.\] If $\mathcal{P}g$, as defined in Problem 8.10, is dense in $D$ and if, for some $f\in D$, $|f(z)|\geq|g(z)|$ for all $|z|<1$, is it necessarily true that $\mathcal{P}f$ is dense in $D$? The analogous result is true in $H^2$ and in $A^2$. Shields solved the special case $g(z)\equiv1$. (A. L. Shields)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 8.18
record.statement: For which simply-connected domains $D$ (with $0 \in D$) is it true that there is a constant $K = K(D)$ such that $$ {\int\int}_D|f|^2\,dx\,dy\leq K{\int\int}_D|f'|^2\,dx\,dy $$ for all functions $f$ analytic on $D$ with $f(0) = 0$? This inequality ([source label: J8.18]) is known as the analytic Poincar\'e inequality. Courant and Hilbert have given a Jordan domain for which ([source label: J8.18]) is false; and Hummel has given an example of a spiral domain $D$ for which ${\int\int}_D|f|^2\,dx\,dy = \infty$ and ${\int\int}_D|f'|^2\,dx\,dy < \infty$. (D. H. Hamilton)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Compactness of Kőnig-property
record.statement: A hypergraph $H=(V,E)$ has the Kőnig-property if there is a set $\mathcal{D}\subseteq E$ of pairwise disjoint hyperedges such that there is a vertex cover consisting of one vertex from each hyperedge in $\mathcal{D}$. (Using this terminology, Kőnig's theorem says that every finite bipartite graph has the Kőnig-property). R. Aharoni and N. Bowler conjectured independently the following. If $H=(V,E)$ is a hypergraph such that all of its hyperedges are finite and for all finite $E'\subseteq E$ the hypergraph $(V,E')$ has the Kőnig-property, then $H$ has the Kőnig-property as well ( p. 19. Problem 6.7).

record.title: A Burgess-like bound for twisted L-functions
record.statement:
The report states and proves the following theorem: let $f$ be an arbitrary modular form, either holomorphic or Maass, of level $D$ and with some nebentypus, and let $\chi$ be a primitive character of conductor $q$. Then, for $\operatorname{Re}(s)=\tfrac12$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, one has
\[
L(f\otimes\chi,s)\ll_{\varepsilon,f} q^{\frac12-\frac{1-2\theta}{8}},
\]
where $\theta$ is any admissible approximation toward the Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture; the report gives the then-current value $\theta=\tfrac{7}{64}$. The dependence of the implied constant is at most polynomial in the parameters of $f$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/46](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/760), page 41. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Conditional sign changes in the prime-number-theorem error term
record.statement:
Assume the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. For every arbitrarily small but fixed $\\eta>0$ and sufficiently large $N$, if
$$\log^{14}N\le h\le N^{1/7-\varepsilon},$$
then there exist $n_1,n_2\in[N+1,2N]$ such that
$$\psi(n_1+h)-\psi(n_1)-h>\left(\sqrt{1-\frac52\eta}-\eta\right)(h\log N)^{1/2},$$
and
$$\psi(n_2+h)-\psi(n_2)-h<-\left(\sqrt{1-\frac52\eta}-\eta\right)(h\log N)^{1/2}.$$
Here, as stated in the report, $\psi(N)=\sum_{n\le N}\Lambda(n)$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/46](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/760), page 64. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Asymptotics of the magnetic spectral shift function above Landau levels
record.statement:
Assume condition (1) on the potential $V$. Fix $b>0$ and $q\in\mathbb Z_+$. For every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, as $\lambda\downarrow0$,

$$\mp rac1\pi\operatorname{Tr}\arctan\!\left(((1\mp\varepsilon)^2\sqrt{\lambda})^{-1}p_qW_\lambda p_qight)+O(1)\leq \xi(2bq+\lambda;H^\pm,H_0)$$
$$\leq\mp rac1\pi\operatorname{Tr}\arctan\!\left(((1\pm\varepsilon)^2\sqrt{\lambda})^{-1}p_qW_\lambda p_qight)+O(1).$$

Here $p_q$ is the Landau-level projection and $W_\lambda=(w_{ij})_{i,j=1}^2$ is defined by
$$w_{11}(X_\perp)=\int_{\mathbb R}V(X_\perp,x_3)\cos^2(\sqrt\lambda\,x_3)\,dx_3,$$
$$w_{22}(X_\perp)=\int_{\mathbb R}V(X_\perp,x_3)\sin^2(\sqrt\lambda\,x_3)\,dx_3,$$
$$w_{12}(X_\perp)=w_{21}(X_\perp)=\int_{\mathbb R}V(X_\perp,x_3)\cos(\sqrt\lambda\,x_3)\sin(\sqrt\lambda\,x_3)\,dx_3.$$

record.title: Algebraic construction of points in a false Tate curve extension
record.statement: Let $E/\bb Q$ be the elliptic curve $y^2+y=x^3-x^2$ and let $m$ be divisible by $11$ but by no anomalous prime for $E/\bb Q$. The report explains that $E/\bb Q(\sqrt[3^n]{m})$ should have rank exactly $n$ for every $n\ge 1$, with exactly one new Mordell\13Weil generator appearing at each successive extension. The open problem is to give an algebraic construction of these points and thereby explain this phenomenon.

record.title: Kato’s strengthened Lusztig character conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be as in the report, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. For every regular restricted dominant weight $\lambda\in X_1^+\cap X_{\mathrm{reg}}^+$, the Lusztig character formula holds:
\[
\operatorname{ch}L(\lambda)=\chi_{\mathrm{KL}}(\lambda).
\]
Here $X_1^+=\{\lambda\in X^+\mid (\lambda,\alpha^\vee)<p\text{ for every simple root }\alpha\}$, and $\chi_{\mathrm{KL}}(\lambda)$ is the Kazhdan–Lusztig character defined on page 27 of the report.

R=I+G^*Q_{22}G,
\qquad \widetilde A=A-BR^{-1}G^*Q_{12}^*,
\qquad \widetilde Q=Q_{11}-Q_{12}GR^{-1}G^*Q_{12}^*,
\]
and
\[
\widetilde M=M_{11}-M_{12}M_{22}^{-1}M_{12}^*.
\]
Then
\[
\widetilde M\ge 0,
\]
so, for every initial condition $x_0\in X$, the two-point problem without the compatibility condition,
\[
\begin{cases}
 x(0)=x_0,\\
 \dot x=\widetilde A x-BR^{-1}B^*p,\\
 \dot p=-\widetilde A^*p-\widetilde Qx,\\
 p(T)=\widetilde Mx(T),
\end{cases}
\]
is solvable. Moreover, $x(T)$ is a linear and continuous function of $x_0$.

record.title: Postnikov’s conjecture on Bruhat intervals and inversion-arrangement regions
record.statement: For each inversion $i<j$ of a permutation $pi\in S_n$, meaning $pi(i)>\u007fpi(j)$, let the associated hyperplane in $\mathbb{R}^n$ be $x_i=x_j$. Let $r(\u007fpi)$ be the number of regions of the resulting hyperplane arrangement, and let $b(\u007fpi)$ be the number of elements in the closed lower Bruhat interval $[\mathrm{id},\u007fpi]$. Then, for every $n$-permutation $\u007fpi\in S_n$, $b(\u007fpi)\ge r(\u007fpi)$, with equality if and only if $\u007fpi$ avoids the patterns $4231$, $35142$, $42513$, and $351624$.

record.title: Majorization of the modulus of continuity of analytic functions
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bounded domain, let $f$ be analytic in $G$ and continuous on $\overline{G}$, and let $\mu:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be a non-negative non-decreasing majorant, meaning that $\mu(2t)\le 2\mu(t)$ for all $t\ge 0$. Fix $z_1\in\partial G$. If

$$|f(z_1)-f(z_2)|\le \mu(|z_1-z_2|)\qquad(z_2\in\partial G),$$

then

$$|f(z_1)-f(z_2)|\le 3456\,\mu(|z_1-z_2|)\qquad(z_2\in G).$$

Thus the question of whether the boundary estimate extends to interior points with an absolute constant is answered affirmatively.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2007/09](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1460), page 21. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Boundary majorization of the modulus of continuity for analytic functions
record.statement: Let $G$ be a bounded domain, let $f$ be analytic in $G$ and continuous on $\\overline{G}$, and let $\mu:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be non-negative and non-decreasing with $\mu(2t)\le 2\mu(t)$ for all $t\ge 0$. For a fixed $z_1\in\partial G$, assume that $|f(z_1)-f(z_2)|\le\mu(|z_1-z_2|)$ for every $z_2\in\partial G$. Does there exist an absolute constant $C$ such that $|f(z_1)-f(z_2)|\le C\mu(|z_1-z_2|)$ for every $z_2\in G$? The report states that the answer is yes, with $C=3456$.

record.title: Unbounded Mordell–Weil ranks for elliptic curves with prescribed rational torsion
record.statement: For the fifteen torsion groups \(T\) occurring in Mazur’s theorem—namely \(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\) for \(1\le N\le 10\) or \(N=12\), and \((\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)\oplus(\mathbb Z/2N\mathbb Z)\) for \(1\le N\le 4\)—is it known whether infinitely many rank values \(r\) occur for elliptic curves \(E/\mathbb Q\) with torsion group \(T\)? Equivalently, is the corresponding \(\limsup\) of the Mordell–Weil ranks infinite for some, or for all, of these \(T\)?

record.title: Sharp threshold for Ricci-flow-invariant curvature cones
record.statement: Conjecture: Theorem 1 remains valid with the threshold dimension set to $n_0=12$. Namely, for every $n\ge 12$, if $n$ is even then $C_{d(n)}$ is invariant under the Ricci flow, while if $n$ is odd then $C_{d(n)+\varepsilon(n)}$ is invariant for some $\varepsilon(n)\in[-\varepsilon_1(n),\varepsilon_2(n)]$, where $d(n)=\sqrt{2(n-2)(n-1)}$ and $\varepsilon_1(n),\varepsilon_2(n)>0$ are the quantities specified in Theorem 1.

record.title: Weighted fractional matroid matching
record.statement:
Given a matroid $M=(S,r)$, a set $E$ of subsets of $S$ (called lines), each of rank $1$ or $2$, and nonnegative weights $w\in\mathbb{R}_+^E$, maximize $w\cdot x$ over vectors $x:E\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying
\[
x\ge 0,
\qquad \sum_{e\in E} d_K(e)x(e)\le r(K)\quad\text{for every }K\subseteq S,
\]
where
\[
d_K(e)=\begin{cases}0,&e\cap K=\varnothing,\\2,&e\subseteq K,\\1,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]
The report presents the associated complexity question—whether arbitrary-weight fractional matroid matching can be optimized in polynomial time—as open on page 27, and then settles it on page 28 with a polynomial-time algorithm (Theorem 4).
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/51](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/2489), page 26. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Uniform positive definiteness of the force-based QCF operator
record.statement:
For the periodic one-dimensional atomistic/continuum model described on PDF page 32, the atomistic and local QC Hessians are uniformly positive definite as $N\to\infty$ if and only if $\phi''(1)+4\phi''(2)>0$. The natural question is whether the linearized force-based QCF operator $L$ inherits this property. The report answers negatively: if $\phi''(2)\ne0$, then
\[
\inf_{\|u'\|_{\ell^2_\varepsilon}=1}\langle Lu,u\rangle\sim -N^{1/2}\qquad\text{as }N\to\infty.
\]
Thus $L$ is not uniformly positive definite (indeed, it is eventually non-coercive).
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/42](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4085), page 33. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Diophantine approximation on the Hilbert modular group
record.statement: Let $K$ be a totally real number field, let $V$ be its set of places, let $O$ be its ring of integers, and let $S$ be a proper subset of the infinite places. With the height $H$ and local distance $\\|x-y\\|_v$ defined in the report, the authors state that, assuming the Ramanujan–Petersson conjectures, for almost every $x=(x_v)_{v\in S}\in\prod_{v\in S}\operatorname{SL}_2(K_v)$, every $\delta>0$, and sufficiently small $\epsilon_v>0$, there is $z\in\operatorname{SL}_2(O)$ such that $\\|x_v-z\\|_v\leq\epsilon_v$ for every $v\in S$ and $H(z)\leq\prod_{v\in S}\epsilon_v^{-3/2-\delta}$. The exponent $3/2$ is asserted to be best possible. The report also gives the unconditional replacement exponent $27/14$ using the best estimates then known toward Ramanujan–Petersson.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/29](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4410), page 15. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Sharp upper bound for the first positive Thue–Morse value along multiples
record.statement:
Let $t=(t_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be the Thue–Morse sequence, with $t_n=(-1)^{s_2(n)}$, and for $k\ge 1$ define $N_k=\{n:t_{kn}=1\}$ and $f(k)=\min\{n:n\in N_k\}$. Theorem 49 asserts that, for all $k\ge 1$, $f(k)\le k+4$. Moreover:

1. $f(k)=k+4$ if and only if $k=2^{2^r}-1$ for some $r\ge 1$.
2. There is no $k$ such that $f(k)=k+3$ or $f(k)=k+2$.
3. $f(k)=k+1$ if and only if $k=6$.
4. $f(k)=k$ if and only if $k=1$ or $k=2^r+1$ for some $r\ge 2$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/37](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4425), page 44. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Infinitely many Riccati-equation solutions from skew-conjugate spectral subspaces
record.statement:
Under the setting (a)–(c) on page 35, suppose that $(A,B)$ is approximately controllable and that $A$ has no non-observable eigenvalues on the imaginary axis. Then:

1. $\csigma(T)\cap i\mathbb{R}=\varnothing$.
2. For every skew-conjugate subset $\csigma\subset\u0005csigma(T)$, there exists a selfadjoint operator $X$ on $H$ and a dense subspace $D\subset D(X)$ such that $W_{\u0005csigma}=\u0005cGamma(X)$ and
   $$X(Av-BB^*Xv)=-C^*Cv-A^*Xv,\qquad v\in D.$$

Since there are infinitely many possible choices for $\u0005csigma$, this yields infinitely many solutions $X$ of the Riccati equation. The solution corresponding to the spectrum in the left half-plane is nonnegative, and the one corresponding to the spectrum in the right half-plane is nonpositive.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/56](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4538), page 35. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Grove’s finiteness question for rational homotopy types
record.statement: Let \(\mathcal M_{\le D}^{-1\le \sec\le +1}(n)\) denote the class of simply connected \(n\)-manifolds with diameter at most \(D\) and sectional curvature satisfying \(-1\le \sec\le +1\). Does this class contain only finitely many rational homotopy types? The report presents a negative answer: for every \(n\ge 22\), there exists \(D>0\) such that \(\mathcal M_{\le D}^{-1\le \sec\le +1}(n)\) contains infinitely many rational homotopy types; Totaro’s result gives the same conclusion in dimension \(7\).

record.title: Historical growth conjecture for partial-match queries in random quadtrees
record.statement:
For a two-dimensional random quadtree built from independent uniformly distributed points in $[0,1]^2$, let $C_n(s)$ be the complexity of the partial-match query $(s,*)$, and let $U$ be an independent uniform random variable on $[0,1]$. The historical conjecture that $\mathbb{E}[C_n(U)]$ has order $\sqrt{n}$ is false. In fact, the report states that
\[
\mathbb{E}[C_n(U)]\sim \kappa n^\beta,
\qquad \beta=\frac{\sqrt{17}-3}{2},
\qquad \kappa=\frac{\Gamma(2\beta+2)}{2\,\Gamma(\beta+1)^3}.
\]
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/23](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/5151), page 36. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Compactness for the Yamabe problem on manifolds with umbilic boundary
record.statement:
Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold of dimension $3\le n\le 24$ with umbilic boundary, and suppose that $(M,g)$ is not conformally equivalent to the standard hemisphere $(S^n_+,g_0)$. For $K>0$, define
\[
\Phi_p=\left\{u>0\ \middle|\ L_g u+K u^p=0\ \text{ in }M,\quad B_g u=0\ \text{ on }\partial M\right\},
\qquad 1+\varepsilon\le p\le \frac{n+2}{n-2}.
\]
Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a constant $C>0$, depending only on $g$ and $\varepsilon$, such that every $u\in\bigcup_{1+\varepsilon\le p\le (n+2)/(n-2)}\Phi_p$ satisfies
\[
C^{-1}\le u\le C,\qquad \|u\|_{C^{2,\alpha}(M)}\le C,
\]
where $0<\alpha<1$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/27](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11789), page 25. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Weyl vanishing for boundary Yamabe blow-up
record.statement:
Let $g$ be a smooth Riemannian metric defined in the unit half $n$-ball $B_1^+$, with $6\le n\le 24$. Suppose there is a sequence of positive solutions $\{u_i\}$ of
\[
L_g u_i+K u_i^{p_i}=0\quad\text{in }B_1^+,
\qquad B_g u_i=0\quad\text{on }B_1^+\cap\mathbb{R}^{n-1},
\]
where $K>0$ and $p_i\in\left(1,\frac{n+2}{n-2}\right]$, such that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a constant $C(\varepsilon)>0$ satisfying
\[
\sup_{B_1^+\setminus B_\varepsilon^+}u_i\le C(\varepsilon),
\qquad \lim_{i\to\infty}\sup_{B_1^+}u_i=\infty.
\]
Assume also that $B_1^+\cap\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$ is umbilic. Then the Weyl tensor $W_g$ satisfies
\[
|W_g|(x)\le C|x|^{\ell}
\]
for some integer $\ell>\frac{n-6}{2}$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/27](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11789), page 26. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Extension of Guo’s Lipschitz-curve result beyond $L^2$
record.statement: Let $B=B_{1/2}(1,0)\subset\mathbb R^2$. Suppose that $h:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ is Lipschitz and satisfies $\|\nabla h(x_1,x_2)-(1,0)\|\leq \tfrac12$ for almost every $(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2$. Let $u$ be measurable and suppose $v(x_1,x_2)=(1,u(h(x_1,x_2)))\in B$ almost everywhere. For the Hilbert transform $H_v f(x)=\operatorname{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb R} f(x-tv(x))\,\frac{dt}{t}$, can Guo’s $L^2$ estimate be extended to the same exponent range as Theorem 24, namely $\tfrac32<p<\infty$, so that $\|H_vf\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)}\leq C_p\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)}$ for all test functions $f$?

record.title: Uniform domination for proper left-right actions on a real rank-one Lie group
record.statement: Let $G$colon be a real rank-one semisimple Lie group, and let $\93< G\times G$ be finitely generated and act properly discontinuously on $G$ by left-right multiplication, $(g,h)\cdot x=gxh^{-1}$. After passing to a finite-index subgroup and possibly exchanging the two factors, write $\93$ as a graph $\{(\gamma,j(\gamma))\mid \gamma\in\u000393_0\}$ over a discrete subgroup $\93_0<G$. Is the representation $j\colon \u000393_0\to G$ necessarily uniformly dominated by the inclusion of $\93_0$ into $G$, i.e. does there exist $\kappa\in(0,1)$ such that $\lambda(j(\gamma))\leq\kappa\lambda(\gamma)$ for every infinite-order $\gamma\in\u000393_0$? Here $\lambda(g)=\inf_{x\in X}d_X(x,g\cdot x)$ is the translation length on the negatively curved symmetric space $X$ of $G$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/07](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12867), page 44. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Connectivity for an unlabelled bridge-addable graph class
record.statement: Let \(\mathcal A\) be a class of graphs that is **bridge-addable**, meaning that whenever \(G\in\mathcal A\) has vertices in distinct components, adding an edge between them produces a graph still in \(\mathcal A\). Let \(\mathcal A\) be **decomposable**, meaning that a graph belongs to \(\mathcal A\) if and only if each of its components does. For each \(n\), let \(\widetilde{\mathcal A}_n\) be the set of unlabelled graphs in \(\mathcal A\) on \(n\) vertices, and let \(\widetilde R_n\) be sampled uniformly from \(\widetilde{\mathcal A}_n\). Conjecture: \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\bigl(\widetilde R_n\text{ is connected}\bigr)\ge \tau, \] where \(\tau\approx e^{-0.5226}\approx 0.5930\) is the limiting connectivity constant cited for unlabelled forests.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/12](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12872), page 74. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.
